links.outcome: Calibration of imported risk equations on local Chinese cohort data
links.effect: PCE overestimated risk by 17%, China-PAR underestimated by 10%; K-CVD predicted/observed ratio 0.97. All three equations need formal recalibration for clinical use.
links.quote: PCE overestimated risk by 17%, and China-PAR underestimated risk by 10%.

links.outcome: Brier score after logit recalibration of risk equations
links.effect: Post logit recalibration yielded identical Brier score (0.0116) for all models; authors conclude all three equations need formal recalibration for clinical use.
links.quote: All three equations need formal recalibration for clinical use, and low cut-offs (1-2%) are more suitable for low-risk Chinese adults instead of Western standard thresholds.

links.outcome: Miscalibration from population differences between development and Chinese validation cohorts
links.effect: PCE overestimated risk by 17% and China-PAR underestimated by 10% in the Chinese cohort; K-CVD was best calibrated (P/O 0.97).

links.outcome: Net benefit across decision thresholds in decision curve analysis
links.effect: DCA showed negative net benefit at thresholds ≥5%; PCE and K-CVD slightly superior to China-PAR at 1-2% thresholds matching low event rate.
links.quote: DCA showed negative net benefit at thresholds ≥ 5%; PCE and K-CVD gained slight superiority over China-PAR at 1-2% thresholds matching the low actual event rate.

links.effect: K-CVD had P/O=0.97; PCE overestimated 17%; China-PAR underestimated 10%; AUCs 0.775-0.777, P > 0.05.
links.quote: K-CVD has the best native calibration in this Chinese cohort.
